exactPassages: Sidewalk cafes provided beyond the building line shall comply with the requirements of this section, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and with the projection limitations of Chapter 32 of this code.
No part of any awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment or removable platform of a sidewalk cafe shall be located:

Exception: Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, to cover a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.

testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, DOT authorization, electrical permitting, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, lawful seating capacity, or electrical and operational requirements.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claim is not supported by these passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with this Building Code section but also with the Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioners, and Chapter 32 projection limits. An outdoor-dining authorization therefore does not, on this evidence, eliminate those separate compliance obligations.

The selected obstruction rule applies to a sidewalk café’s awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform: none may obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch or areaway. The supplied passages do not state whether the proposed furniture is a  fixture  or  equipment,  so they do not by themselves determine whether this particular furniture is covered by that rule. If a platform is proposed over the hatch, the only supplied exception is conditional: upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, but only where the cellar entrance or areaway is not used as a required means of egress. The facts provided do not establish that exception.

Accessibility review is not eliminated. The sidewalk café and access to it must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces must be accessible, with at least one accessible dining surface of each type; those surfaces must be distributed throughout the facility and be on a level accessed by an accessible route. Compliance cannot be determined from the available seating/standing counts, dining-surface types, layout, distribution, and route information.

Separate exterior seating cannot yet be accepted for the limited assembly-seating determination addressed here. For an enclosed sidewalk café, its seating must be added to interior seating to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless it is separated from the interior seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713. Whether this café is enclosed—and, if it is, whether a compliant fire partition exists—is unresolved. The supplied text does not create a general rule that all exterior seating can be counted separately, and it does not itself establish whether a certificate is required.

The material unresolved record is the café location relative to the building line; plans showing the exit, hatch/areaway, and each proposed awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment item, or platform; whether the furniture qualifies as a covered fixture or equipment; whether the hatch/areaway is a required means of egress; any special application and commissioner permission for a platform; enclosure and fire-partition details; seating and standing totals, dining-surface types, accessible-surface locations, and accessible route; and the applicable current agency authorizations and requirements.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claim is not supported by these passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with this Building Code section but also with the Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioners, and Chapter 32 projection limits. An outdoor-dining authorization therefore does not, on this evidence, eliminate those separate compliance obligations.
